name: Erlitou and the Xia
place: the Yi and Luo rivers, central China
desc: The first great royal city of China, with palaces on rammed-earth platforms, a grid of roads, the oldest bronze ritual vessels cast in clay moulds and a dragon made of two thousand pieces of turquoise. Many think it was the capital of the Xia, the first dynasty of the old histories.
source: Excavations at Erlitou, Yanshi (from 1959); the Xia dynasty in Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian

cautious: pounded the palace platform layer by layer until it rang like stone
devout: set the last turquoise chip in the dragon's eye
gluttonous: poured millet wine from a bronze jue at the ancestors' feast

inventions.name: Rammed Earth
inventions.source: The palace platforms and walls of Erlitou were built of earth pounded in thin layers between boards (hangtu)
inventions.desc: Earth pounded layer by layer between boards until it is as hard as stone: building is 10% faster, +1 defence.

inventions.name: Piece-Mould Bronzes
inventions.source: Erlitou's bronze jue wine cups, cast in several clay mould sections, are the oldest Chinese bronze vessels
inventions.desc: Bronze poured into clay moulds made in pieces, to cast thin-legged wine cups for the ancestors: rites bring 15% more devotion, +1 mood.
inventions.hint: Needs Bronze Metallurgy, and long rites.

inventions.name: Turquoise Mosaic
inventions.source: The turquoise dragon from tomb 2002VM3 at Erlitou, about 70 cm long, made of over 2,000 pieces
inventions.desc: Thousands of tiny blue-green chips set into a dragon or a plaque: +3 mood, rites bring 5% more devotion.

inventions.name: Road Grid
inventions.source: Erlitou had the oldest known grid of main roads in China, some showing wheel ruts
inventions.desc: Straight roads crossing at right angles between the palace and the workshops: everyone moves 4% faster, +1 mood.

foods.name: Steamed Millet
foods.source: The yan, a pottery steamer with a perforated grate, is an ancient Chinese way of steaming grain
foods.desc: Millet steamed over boiling water in a double pot: hunger grows 10% slower.

foods.name: Soybean Porridge
foods.source: The soybean was domesticated in China from wild soy by about 3000–1000 BCE
foods.desc: Beans boiled soft with millet: hunger grows 5% slower, the hurt heal 5% faster.

finds.name: Turquoise Veins
finds.desc: Sky-blue stone in thin veins, prized above gold by the kings.

finds.name: Wild Soybean
finds.desc: Twining vines with small hairy pods of hard black beans.

people.name: Hou Gong
people.desc: He knows by the sound when a layer of earth is hard enough.
memory: led the song that kept forty rammers pounding in time

people.name: Ji Zhu
people.desc: Her clay moulds fit together so tightly that the bronze never leaks.
memory: cast a jue cup with legs as thin as reeds

people.name: Qi
people.source: Records of the Grand Historian, Annals of Xia
people.desc: The son of Yu the Great, said to be the first king who inherited the throne from his father, beginning the first dynasty.

people.name: The Dragon Bearer
people.source: A noble buried at Erlitou with the turquoise dragon laid along his body and a bronze bell at his waist
people.desc: A man of high rank buried cradling a dragon of turquoise, perhaps a ritual master of the court.

people.name: Yi Ruo
people.source: The Dongyi, 'eastern archers', of the old histories; the Yueshi culture of Shandong lay east of Erlitou
people.text: a bowman from the eastern peoples by the sea, with a bow taller than he is.
memory: shot a wild goose from the sky with a single arrow
people.desc: An archer of the eastern peoples whom the Xia both feared and needed.

people.name: Kongjia
people.label: Kongjia, Raiser of Dragons
people.desc: A king to whom heaven gave two dragons. Lore 7, Foraging 5.

people.name: Shaokang
people.label: Shaokang the Restorer
people.desc: Born in exile, he wins back his father's kingdom. Combat 7, Lore 5.

people.name: Du Kang
people.label: Du Kang, the First Brewer
people.desc: Left-over millet in a hollow tree taught him to make wine. Crafting 7, Foraging 6.

events.title: The Astronomers Were Drunk
events.source: Book of Documents, 'The Punitive Expedition of Yin': the court astronomers Xi and He, drunk, failed to foretell an eclipse
events.text: The sun was eaten and no one was warned. The keepers of the calendar were found asleep beside the wine jars. The chief must decide what to do with them.

options.label: Punish them
options.result: New watchers are named, sober ones. From now on every eclipse is written down.

options.label: Forgive them
options.result: The astronomers swear off wine, for a month or two.

events.title: A Platform for the Palace
events.source: Palace no. 1 at Erlitou stood on a rammed-earth platform about 100 m square
events.text: The chief wants a great hall on a platform of pounded earth, with a courtyard where all the people can gather before the ancestors.

options.label: Build the platform

do.feat: Raised a palace on a rammed-earth platform

options.result: Thousands of baskets of earth, pounded to the beat of drums. The hall stands high over the river.

options.label: Huts are enough
options.result: The chief lives like everyone else, for now.

events.title: The Nine Cauldrons
events.source: Zuo Zhuan: Yu cast nine bronze cauldrons from metal sent by the nine provinces; whoever held them held the mandate
events.text: The smiths propose to cast great cauldrons, one for each region the tribe knows, with the beasts of each land on its sides, so the people will know what is good and what is evil in every place.

tales.name: Qi Brings Music from Heaven
tales.source: Shanhai Jing, Classic of the Great Wilderness: West
tales.text: Qi, son of Yu, rode two dragons up to heaven three times, and each time came down with something stolen from the gods: the songs called Nine Arguments and Nine Songs. That is how music came to the earth, and why it sounds like heaven.
tales.moral: beauty can be brought down from heaven

tales.name: Kongjia's Dragons
tales.source: Records of the Grand Historian, Annals of Xia
tales.text: Heaven sent King Kongjia a pair of dragons, one male and one female, but no one knew how to raise them. A man named Liu Lei learned from the dragon-keepers and fed them. When the female died, he cooked her and served her to the king, who asked for more. Then Liu Lei ran away.
tales.moral: some gifts are not meant to be kept

tales.name: Yu Tames the Flood
tales.source: Records of the Grand Historian; Mencius
tales.text: For thirteen years Yu worked on the waters. His father had tried to dam them and failed. Yu dug channels instead and led the rivers to the sea. Three times he passed his own door and heard his son crying inside, and three times he did not go in.
tales.moral: guide the water, do not fight it

tales.name: Du Kang and the Hollow Tree
tales.source: Later tradition; Du Kang is honoured as the god of wine
tales.text: A young herdsman left his millet in a hollow mulberry tree and forgot it. Weeks later a sweet smell came out of the tree, and the rainwater inside tasted wonderful. He had made the first wine. 'How shall I drown my sorrow?' the poets say. 'Only with Du Kang.'
